1 hmac.compare_digest on the bearer token. This check,
inside the handler, is the actual gate on the function.
2 boto3 signs InvokeAgent with the execution role's
credentials. Nothing long-lived is stored anywhere.
3 Collapses the returned event stream into one string.

div.b: AuthType NONE is deliberate, and the token is the real gate

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 797px; margin-left: 19px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
A function URL set to AWS_IAM would need the caller to sign the
request, which is the thing the platform cannot do. Hence NONE,
with the bearer check moved inside the handler.
Treat the result as internet-reachable and gated by one secret.
Rotate the token at the end of the engagement and delete the
function URL once scanning is finished, the same as you would
retire any other test target.

div.b: Two details that cost an afternoon each

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 648px; height: 1px; padding-top: 797px; margin-left: 719px;
box-sizing: border-box; font-size: 0; text-align: left; color: #333333;
display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: #333333; line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Use a real alias, not TSTALIASID. The draft test alias points at
whatever is currently in the console editor, so a scan against it is
not reproducible. Find the agent id under Agents, and the alias id
in the Aliases section beneath it.
Give the agent time to answer. A prompt that sets the agent off
calling tools takes far longer than a model completion, which is
why the client is built with a 120-second read timeout.

div.div: Test the bridge with curl until it returns HTTP 200 before opening the console. The wizard reports only that validation failed, so every problem you carry in with you is harder to diagnose there than it was in your terminal.
